sections.title: Always Together Arrangement
sections.content:
When two or more persons/objects must always stay together:
Step 1: Consider them as one group (block).
Step 2: Find the new total number of units.
Step 3: Arrange the new units.
Step 4: Multiply by the internal arrangements within the group.
Example: Among 5 people, A and B must always stay together.
Step 1: (AB) is one unit → total 4 units.
Step 2: 4! ways.
Step 3: Internal arrangement of A and B = 2!.
Final answer = 4! × 2!

sections.title: Never Together
sections.content:
Step 1: First find the total arrangements.
Step 2: Then find the arrangements where they are together.
Step 3: Subtract from the total.
Example: Among 5 people, A and B must never sit together.
Total = 5!
Together = 4! × 2!
Final = 5! − (4! × 2!)

sections.title: Gap Method
sections.content:
Used when certain people must not sit together:
Step 1: Arrange the main group first.
Step 2: Count the gaps formed between them.
Step 3: Place the remaining people in the gaps.
Example: 3 men and 2 women, women should not sit together.
Step 1: Arrange 3 men → 3! ways.
Step 2: 4 gaps are formed (_ M _ M _ M _)
Step 3: Place 2 women in 4 gaps in 4C2 × 2! ways.

sections.title: Circular Permutation (Round Table Arrangement)
sections.content:
Arrangement of n people around a round table = (n-1)!
Because rotation does not create a new arrangement.
Example: 6 people around a round table → (6-1)! = 5!
If forming a necklace/garland where direction is also considered the same:
Formula = (n-1)! / 2

sections.title: Committee Formation
sections.content:
If we need to choose 3 men and 2 women from 5 men and 4 women:
Step 1: Men selection = 5C3
Step 2: Women selection = 4C2
Step 3: Multiply → 5C3 × 4C2

If the condition is 'at least 1 woman':
Case 1: 1 woman
Case 2: 2 women
Add all cases.

sections.title: Distribution of Distinct Objects
sections.content:
If 4 different books are distributed between 2 students:
Each book has 2 choices → 2^4 ways.
If each student must get at least 1 book:
Total = 2^4 − 2 (cases where one student gets all books).

sections.title: Unequal Grouping
sections.content:
If 5 different students are divided into groups of 2 and 3:
Step 1: Choose the group of 2 using 5C2.
Step 2: The remaining 3 form the other group automatically.
If groups do not have names, do not divide by extra factorial.

sections.title: Derangements (No One in Correct Position)
sections.content:
If 3 letters go into 3 wrong envelopes:
Total arrangements = 3! = 6
Subtract arrangements where letters are in the correct place.
Derangement formula: !n ≈ n! × (1 − 1/1! + 1/2! − 1/3! ...)
Remember small values:
!2 = 1
!3 = 2
!4 = 9

sections.title: Avoid Overcounting
sections.content:
When groups are identical (for example, 2 identical teams), divide by extra factorial.
Always check whether the same arrangement is being counted more than once.

tricks.title: Always Together Block Trick
tricks.explanation: Treat two persons as one unit, then multiply by 2! for internal arrangement.

tricks.title: Fast Gap Method
tricks.explanation: Arrange the main group first, gaps = n+1, then choose positions.

tricks.title: Necklace Trick
tricks.explanation: If direction is considered the same → (n-1)!/2

tricks.title: Exact Selection Trick
tricks.explanation: If selection is from different groups, take separate nCr and multiply.

tricks.title: At Least Case Trick
tricks.explanation: For 'at least', create different cases and add them.

tricks.title: Check Overcounting
tricks.explanation: If groups are identical, divide by factorial.
